proposal.summary: LearnPress WordPress plugin 4.1.4.1 allows an authenticated user who can upload and crop an avatar to specify an arbitrary file path in the lp-user-avatar-crop[name] POST parameter, causing the server to rename an arbitrary image file under /wp-content/uploads/ to an MD5-based name.
proposal.cwe_quote: Change the value of the `lp-user-avatar-crop[name]` parameter to an arbitrary image file path that is in the website (example, /2021/01/image.png or /../../image.png). The path is relative to "/wp-content/uploads/".

PR.quote: Register and login to the learnpress system.

UI.quote: While saving the image, intercept the POST request by a local proxy tool such as Burpsuite.

C.quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file. By doing this, he/she can destroy the design of the web site.

A.quote: An attacker can use this vulnerability in order to rename an arbitrary image file. By doing this, he/she can destroy the design of the web site.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the vulnerability on a test instance, confirm exactly which file paths can be targeted and whether directory traversal is possible beyond wp-content/uploads, and prepare a patch or input validation restricting lp-user-avatar-crop[name] to allowed filenames within the user's own upload directory.

evidence_quotes.claim: Endpoint used to save uploaded avatar via POST
Attack requires authenticated user (register and login)

evidence_quotes.claim: Exploit changes lp-user-avatar-crop[name] to arbitrary path relative to uploads

evidence_quotes.claim: Impact is renaming arbitrary image file and breaking site design
